## Active

### D-028 — The mongodb adapter adds a string id to every document

> _2026-08-23 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Mongo `_id` is an ObjectId, which scalar flattening drops, so the commander had no unique label or
key for a row. The adapter's `{...doc, id: String(_id)}` is an intentional, small contract change;
the CRUD test mask and the mongodb tap snapshots were updated to match. Tap snapshots are
order-sensitive, so `id` has to be the LAST field of the projected document.

### D-043 — A later validation file replaces an earlier one for the same method

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Registry._validations()` now replaces a later-registered validation per `methodParts` key — the
plan's primary option — instead of adding an explicit `override` flag on gateway files. Replacement
is minimal and deterministic, and it also fixes the ut-function.merge TypeBox `Kind`-symbol
corruption where nested `details` arrays threw "Unknown type". No existing code relied on same-key
merging.

### D-044 — $subject/$object placeholders are resolved by the framework

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The kopi template's `$subject`/`$object` placeholder names are valid identifiers everywhere they
appear, so a scaffold-time content rewrite was rejected and the fix is framework-side. `methodParts`
in `lib.ts` and `capitalize` (four call sites) became `$`-aware, which makes the derived names
consistent with the `$subject$Object...` file names. This is the "stripping/absorbing the `$` at the
proper places" that was asked for.

### D-045 — The graceful-shutdown timer bounds the stop, not the run

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The 30-second timer was moved from handler creation into the signal handler. Left where it was, it
self-destructed any long-running `blong`/`blong-watch` server 30 seconds after start — the root
cause of the Playwright webServer backend dying mid-run.

### D-046 — `remove` deletes FK-constrained detail rows before the master

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

A master with children could not be deleted because the foreign key was non-cascading. The generic
`remove` now deletes FK-constrained detail rows first, which is consistent with `edit` replacing its
children.

### D-047 — Three framework warnings turn silent stalls into named methods

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Permanent, intent-agnostic diagnostics that gate themselves on trouble: `Registry._matchMethods`
warns when a handler factory exceeds 3 seconds and names the method; `Remote` warns when a
`canSkipSocket` lookup finds no local method; and `blong-server/subject.ts` warns when a derived
model handler name matches no registered file, naming the closest match. These would have pinpointed
the `$`-mismatch hang and the `_validations()` stall immediately instead of after an investigation.

### D-048 — The gogo-kopi cycle is broken by moving createRealm into gogo

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`blong-kopi` must stay a runnable, testable realm — its `index.test.ts` loads `blong-gogo`, and it
demonstrates RBAC through `blong-access` — so the cycle had to break elsewhere. The root cause was a
`gogo`/`kopi` two-cycle plus access: `gogo.deps → blong-kopi` (scaffolder re-export),
`kopi.devDeps → gogo`, `kopi.devDeps → access`, `access.devDeps → gogo`, introduced when kopi gained
its framework devDependencies. The chosen fix (option 1) dropped `gogo → kopi`: `blong-gogo` now
owns `createRealm` (`src/kopi.ts`, moved from `blong-kopi/kopi.ts`) and resolves the template from
either the monorepo sibling `core/blong-kopi` or a publish-bundled `template/` generated ONLY at
publish time by `scripts/copy-template.mjs` (gitignored, shipped through gogo's `.npmignore`). gogo
is a sink; `blong-dev`/`blong-kopi`/`access` form a chain with no back-edge, `rush update` succeeds,
kopi tap is 6/6 and blong-gogo 259 pass. The `blong-kopi/kopi.ts` twin kept at the time for direct
use was later deleted because it had ZERO consumers (the CLI's `bin/blong.ts` and the runtime's
`load.ts` both import gogo's `src/kopi.ts`), and the template file enumeration moved into a shared
`core/blong-gogo/src/template-files.ts` (`TEMPLATE_FILES_IGNORE` plus `listTemplateFiles`) used by
both `src/kopi.ts` and `scripts/copy-template.mjs`, so the two can no longer drift.

### D-049 — Resource-backed CRUD and graph edges are opt-in in the knex exec

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

blong-access had about 18 `adapter/db` handlers that only did resource-backed CRUD
(`coreResourceEnsure` on add, a name join on find/get, resource rename on edit, cascade on remove,
and `core_triple` `hasRole`/`hasCapability`/`hasAction` edge sync), so the built-in knex `exec`
absorbs them, opt-in via `ISchemaTable.resource: true` and `ISchemaTable.edges[]`. `add` generates
server-side PKs for `uuid`/`ulid` default markers and for resource-backed not-null PKs (FK to
`core.resource`, no default, PK absent), creates `core_type` plus `core_resource`, strips the
virtual `${object}Name` from the insert and joins the name onto the result; `find`/`get` join the
name, `edit` renames the resource, and `remove` cascades entity row to resource row plus the
declared edges (including `reverse` bindings). Because it is opt-in, realms that declare nothing are
unaffected; role CRUD is now fully generic (10 handlers deleted) while the user and capability
handlers stay custom. `exec` also gained `ulid` handling, and the `uidNotNull`-PK caveat is
documented in the blong-schema skill. Fixed on the way: the remove order (FK), a reverse-only edge
binding clobbering the master key, the edge name join on Buffers, and a missing `${object}Name` on
the add result. Verified: tap 22/22, Playwright 19/19, both packages' lint.

### D-050 — The exec `get` lost its edges to an in-place row mutation

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The new integration tests found a real bug: `get` read `masterKey = row?.[keyName]` AFTER
`prepareResultRow(row, …)` had mutated the row in place (Buffer to base64 string), so
`Buffer.isBuffer(masterKey)` was false and the declared edges were never attached. Fixed by
capturing the raw PK before the mutation. `resolveTableSpec` was also widened to accept an
`undefined` tableConfig.

### D-060 — The access audit id reaches the handler via an awaited preHandler

> _2026-08-20 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`access.audit.record` now returns `{inserted, auditIds}` with the ULID keys it generated.
`recordAccessAudit` in `core/blong-gogo/src/jwt.ts` sets the first one on
`request.auth.credentials.auditId`, and the gateway's `_meta()` spreads credentials into the
handler's `$meta.auth`, so `$meta.auth.auditId` is available to the business handler. To make the id
reliable the preHandler hook now AWAITS the audit insert where it used to fire and forget: failures
are still caught and never fail the request, but every access-checked request pays a database write
on the request path. Denied (403) requests are still audited before the error is thrown, so both
outcomes are recorded, and the id is per-request only because the credentials object is re-created —
the bearer cache is not polluted. Verified: tap access 37/37 (including the new `auditIds` ULID
assertion), gateway 20/20, party 15/15, kopi 6/6, Playwright 21 passed.

### D-061 — Transient MySQL connection loss is retried in the knex adapter

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Intermittent `PROTOCOL_CONNECTION_LOST` (`fatal: true`) in GitHub Actions failed random packages,
one or more at a time. MySQL is a k8s Deployment in k3d (`mysql/mysql-server:8.0.32`, 768Mi,
`max_connections=151` defaults) and the knex adapter had no pool tuning, no keepalive and no retry,
so a single transient drop during schema sync or seeding was fatal. The adapter
(`core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/schema/knex/json.ts`) gained `isRetryableConnectionError` plus
`withConnectionRetry`, which re-executes builders through `clone()` and `raw()` by re-invocation
with linear backoff, gated by an explicit `knex.retry` config enabled ONLY in the `ci`/`dev` blocks
of the shared `srv.db` adapter (`core/blong-server/adapter/db.ts`) and never in prod; mysql2
`enableKeepAlive` and tarn's `pool.maxConnectionLifetimeMillis` are enabled in the same non-prod
blocks. An `onConnectionError` logging hook (`logKnexConnectionError`) reports diagnostics even when
retry is off. v1 does NOT retry whole transactions, only inner builder and raw queries, to avoid
re-running user callbacks with external side effects, and MySQL's `max_connections` and memory were
left alone until diagnostics show `ER_CON_COUNT_ERROR` (1040) or OOMKilled, because the observed
signature points to a pod restart or an idle drop rather than connection exhaustion. Verified: full
blong-gogo `tsc --noEmit` green, 89/89 tap tests including the new retry and connection-error cases,
`ci-lint` clean on the changed files.

### D-062 — The redis adapter's stop() must disconnect, not only quit

> _2026-09-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The redis adapter's `stop()` called `quit()` on a lazy or still-connecting ioredis client, which
left the 6379 socket open and made tap exit with `timeout!`. `adapter/server/redis.ts` now calls
`disconnect()` after `quit()` — best-effort and idempotent.

### D-101 — Introspection is data-only and optional on the registry interfaces

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Registry.describe()` and `Watch.describe()` return plain serializable data (realms, ports, groups,
folders, files) from `IRegistry` and `IGateway` as optional methods, so existing implementations and
mocks stay valid. `Watch` gained a separate `#discoveredFiles` map rather than being asked to expose
`#handlerFiles`, because the latter drives hot-reload decisions and must not change.

### D-111 — Process lifetime became per-intent config instead of a CI check

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`runServer` now asks `platform.exit` instead of evaluating
`process.env.CI && !intents.includes('playwright')` in two places. The flag is declared per intent
in `load.ts`'s synthetic config: `integration` keeps `Boolean(process.env.CI)` so CI stays the
single source for that intent, `playwright: {exit: false}` retires the last hardcoded intent-name
string, and `db` and `cli` are `true`. It is resolved onto `IRegistry.exit` right before `load()`
returns, next to where `api.configRuntime` is attached, because the runner only ever holds the
registry and something had to carry the value across.

### D-112 — A framework intent's false survives every later source merge

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The standalone-realm wrapper's convenience ports were defeating `cli`. Rather than pattern-match
intent names, the resolved framework configs are retained and any top-level `false` they declare is
re-applied after the merge. Only `cli` sets top-level `false`s today, so the rule has no effect on
any existing intent, but it states the right invariant: an intent that switches a component off must
not be overridable by a template's defaults.

### D-113 — The cli intent disables listeners and watching, not the load

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`gateway`, `rpcServer`, `apiGateway`, `restFs`, `systemDebug`, `mcp` and `resolution` are `false`,
and `watch: {enabled: false}` is used deliberately rather than `watch: false`, because the load step
that records handler folders and files — the data behind `Registry.describe()` and therefore behind
`method.find` and `tree.find` — runs in `Watch.start` regardless; only chokidar is gated by
`enabled`. Dispatch stays in-process through `remote: {canSkipSocket: true}`. Verified by running
`blong cli` against a minimal suite: exit 0 and nothing bound, while a default run still opens the
rpc server and the gateway.

### D-114 — The CI check is a browser-safe function, not a ci intent block

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The browser bundle loads `load.ts` too, so `Boolean(process.env.CI)` threw
`ReferenceError: process is not defined` and broke the entire browser platform. The tempting fix was
to stop reading the environment and drive the flag from the `ci` intent, which `runServer.ts`
already injects, through a `ci: {exit: true}` block. That was rejected: intents are merged in
command-line order, so a `ci` block setting `exit` would override `playwright: {exit: false}`
whenever the Playwright runner adds its intent before `ci`, silently breaking Playwright in CI. The
chosen fix is `isCI()` reading `globalThis.process?.env?.['CI']` — a function, not a module
constant, so the tests that set `process.env.CI` at runtime still pass; a constant is captured at
import time and would have failed `exit.intent.test.ts` and its nine tests.

### D-115 — The cli intent currently only supports a realm-only suite

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The claim that `cli` is framework-level, so any realm or suite is drivable from a terminal, was
verified false as written: `blong-login/orchestrator/login/token.ts` reads `gateway.config()` at
handler-creation time, and `cli` sets `gateway: false`, so any suite containing the auth realm fails
to load with a `TypeError` reading `config` — reproduced in `demo/handler-test-poc`. The intent's
real contract today is "a realm-only suite", which is what Stage 4 needs: `core/blong-kukum/cli.ts`
is the kukum realm alone and `blong cli` there exits 0. If `cli` should ever work on a full suite,
fix `blong-login` to read the gateway lazily rather than weakening `cli`, because a config-only
gateway would re-open the question of which components `cli` switches off — the question the
false-wins rule exists to settle.

### D-116 — A library function's this now carries platform and registry

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Registry._createHandlers` seeds `lib` with `error`, `assert`, `render`, `timing` and
`@feasibleone/blong-lib`, and that object is what `this` is inside a `library()` function. The plan
assumed `this` would be the port with no framework change, which was measured false: the lib proxy
hands an attached function back raw and only binds `port` in its not-yet-attached fallback path,
confirmed by a throwaway probe. Rather than accept an inconsistent `this` that works only for
not-yet-attached libraries, `platform: this.#platform` and `registry: this` were added, mirroring
the port API which already exposed both. This is what lets a library function reach the platform at
all, which the modular-CLI goal needs, since a `library()` factory is given only `config`,
`handler`, `errors`, `schema`, `gateway` and `apiSchema`. Blast radius is two additive keys on one
object, verified against the full `blong-gogo` suite and lint; the rejected alternative was passing
the platform as an explicit parameter through every binding.

### D-117 — The cli intent loads the handler-bearing layers too

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Without this, a `cli` process loaded a realm with no handler layers, because `WELL_KNOWN_LAYERS`
bound them to `integration` only, so there was nothing to dispatch to. `cli` still skips the
listeners, the watcher and the test machinery; it just no longer skips the realm. Fixing it in the
layer map rather than by passing `['cli','integration']` to `load` was deliberate: the false-wins
reconciliation forces any top-level `false` from a framework config, and `integration.exit` is
`isCI()` — false outside CI — so the extra intent would have silently cancelled `cli`'s
`exit: true`. Follow-up: the two prose tables that mirror this map, `_shared/conventions.md` under
`[LAYER_DEFAULTS_TABLE]` and `docs/concepts/layer.md`, still show `integration` only.

### D-118 — A CLI resolves its method with findHandler, not the prefix match

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Remote` is not reachable from the registry's public surface, but `findHandler` resolves the same
entry `Remote._findMethod` would. The guard must be `findHandler` returning a function, because
`handles()` matches only the namespace prefix and answers `true` for `kukum.bogus.thing`, so it
cannot distinguish a real method. Calling the handler directly skips gateway validation and
checkpoints, which a CLI does not need: it constructs its own parameters, and kukum is
unauthenticated.

### D-119 — CLI results own stdout, and framework logs are configured down

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

pino writes to fd 1 directly, so overriding `process.stdout.write` — the obvious trick — does not
catch framework logs; that was verified by trying it. Instead the `cli` path sets
`{log: {level: 'warn'}, apiSchema: {logLevel: 'warn'}}` on the suite and `{cli: {logLevel: 'warn'}}`
on the orchestrator, whose `default` block asks for `info`. `--output=json` therefore stays
parseable while real warnings still surface.

### D-139 — The CLI plumbing moved into blong-gogo, component log levels did not

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`core/blong-gogo/src/cli.ts` (exported as `@feasibleone/blong-gogo/cli.ts`) now owns what
`bin/kukum.ts` had hand-rolled: `parseArgv` and `wantsHelp`, `resolveMethod` including the
`handles()` prefix versus `findHandler()` distinction, `isCliEntry`, and `runCli`, which does help
and usage, `load(suite, name, name, ['cli'])`, start, dispatch, keeps stdout for the result while
forwarding everything else to stderr, handles `--output=json|text` with the TTY default, exit codes
and `registry.stop()` in a `finally`. `bin/kukum.ts` went from 273 to about 200 lines, almost all of
it kukum's own usage text, argument-to-method mapping and result rendering, and the new
`bin/blong-cli.ts` demo is about 90 lines. The `cli` intent block in `load.ts` also defaults
`log: {level: 'warn'}` and `apiSchema: {logLevel: 'warn'}`, so a realm no longer has to remember
them. A component's own `logLevel` was deliberately NOT moved: it lives in the component's
`activation` and the framework does not know component names, so every command-driven component
still declares `cli: {logLevel: 'warn'}` and the rule is documented in
`docs/blong/docs/patterns/cli.md` rather than changed. Verified: CLI output byte-identical to the
pre-extraction baseline, kukum 490 of 490, blong-gogo 261 pass and 6 skip.

### D-175 — ACL enforcement has two entry points and one error family

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The generic CRUD gates get/edit/remove (403 acl.denied, 404 acl.notFound for reads so existence is
not leaked), filters find before paging and filters the auto-bound dropdown lists; add is checked
against the scope named by the tables addScope declaration. Realm handlers reach the same SQL
through the adapter port (aclCheck, aclFilter) because the runtime package is not a library
dependency of a realm. Both throw the same acl.\* error names declared in the realm error map and in
the adapter error map, so a caller sees one name wherever the check runs.

### D-178 — Self-scoped tables guard records whose scope points at them

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · active_

party.organization cannot use the forward scope form: the graph is unit --belongsTo--> organization,
so an organization has no scope edge, would count as unscoped, and would fall back to RBAC (i.e.
stay unguarded). Reverse traversal (enumerating the units that belong to it) was rejected: the scope
of an organization IS the organization, and the unit-to-org direction only says which units it owns.
acl.selfScope: true therefore makes the record its own scope - scope set = the record plus its
parent scopes through access.effectiveScope - with no unscoped fallback. Admin holds the
organization scope in the party seed, which is what makes the two seeded organizations
differentiate.

### D-181 — Wildcard ACL rule: targetKind all anchored on the access.any node

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Approved by the user as option A. An access_acl row with targetKind all matches every record of
every guarded table, in the record and scope paths and on add; targetId points at a bare sentinel
resource named (all records) of type access.any so the foreign key and the ACL Rules page stay
uniform, and core.resource.ensure now supports a table-less bare node. A deny still wins over it.
The access realm seeds an allow-all rule for the Admin role over the guarded party actions in its
production reference data, so an administrator is never narrowed - which is also what makes a newly
created organization readable by its creator. test.acl.flow keeps its out-of-scope proofs by adding
a testViewer login (a principal with no grant) and by writing its own organization deny at runtime.

### D-223 — Call traces get their own channel, gated by config and a signed grant

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Call-phase records (start/end/error/received) currently ride the level API: the gateway's note(),
handlerProxy.recordedCall and AdapterBase.handle all write through port.log.info, so they print
whenever the level admits info, and there is no switch of their own. Owner decisions: (1) they move
to log.calls, a channel on the log internal with phase methods and no level parameter, reached from
a port as port.log.calls - on by default everywhere, stdout off by default and opt-in via config,
with a per-flow opt-out for high-TPS flows, because the flow ledger and the diagrams are built from
these records so there is no fallback if they stop being produced; (2) the per-request capability is
x-blong-grant, a signed-only JWT with {cap, exp}; (3) the gateway verifies it once at the earliest
hook and forwards a plain marker inside meta.forward, downstream processes trust it; (4) it is
minted by a framework CLI intent (blong grant calls) so it ships with the runtime image; (5) the
second cause of the noise is fixed too - SemanticLog.child ignored options.level, so the gateway's
logLevel: warn never silenced it (Gateway.ts passes level to child), and fastify's own request
logging dumped the whole request including the Authorization bearer at info. Opt-out mechanism
concluded: by flow, decided at flow minting from config matched against the entry method, fixed for
the flow's life, carried in meta.forward so every process in the flow agrees, and checked at every
emission point so nothing of an opted-out flow is ever written. Recorded in the flow's config rather
than per call, because a per-call decision could opt out of one hop and leave the rest of a high-TPS
flow recording.

### D-224 — A realm a suite names is no longer loaded twice

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Fixed by recording each realm's url inside loadRealm into a Set carried on the shared api: the
suite's children are realm _factories_, so the parent's wrapper could never read a url off them, and
the framework's frameworkRealms list therefore reloaded every realm a suite had already named (see
the friction entry). Impact to be aware of: each named framework realm was loaded twice, so every
handler group was registered twice and every subject.validation provider twice. Single-loading them
changes _registration order_, which is what made eight blong-access Playwright specs pass again: the
second blong-server copy had been registering server.subject.validation after the realm's explicit
gateway overrides (access.access.validation), so Registry.\_validations() replaced those overrides
with the auto schemas that require capabilityId/roleId/userId. Anything that depended on a doubled
registration - a portal contribution counted twice, a handlerCount of 2 - now behaves as one. The
snapshots that changed for this reason were regenerated deliberately.

### D-225 — Browser realms stay named in a suite's entry

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Asked whether blong-suite/browser.ts could drop the references to blong the way server.ts does,
since the loader auto-includes the framework realms. It cannot, and the asymmetry is structural: the
server's auto-inclusion resolves each specifier at _runtime_ from the suite's location
(createRequire), while a browser suite is bundled by Vite, which has to see the specifier in the
source it transforms - loadBrowser.ts's createRequire throws, resolveFromSuite swallows it and the
realm is skipped silently. A plugin, a virtual module or an import.meta.glob would each build the
edge at _build_ time and were all rejected for the same reason: they only exist under Vite, so the
tap runner (which loads a browser suite through Node, where the loader _can_ resolve) would see a
different graph. Owner decided to leave the browser entry as it is: it keeps one child function per
realm, with the config block and the unused validation entry dropped. Options if this is revisited:
a Vite-side injection in defineBlongViteConfig (framework-owned, invisible to suite authors) beside
the loader's runtime one.

### D-227 — Call records no longer depend on the component's log level

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

A consequence of moving the call records onto their own channel: they used to be written through
port.log.info, which a component above info simply does not have - a port configured at warn
produced no call records at all, silently, and the gateway's notes were only visible because
SemanticLog.child ignored its level option (fixed in the same session). Now the channel is
level-free by construction, so every component that records a call produces the record, and the two
realm baseline screenshots that show record-derived data (blong-template, blong-digest) changed for
that reason and were regenerated deliberately. The template page now shows the gateway's call-error
template with its context (gateway) and the error detail, which is what it showed before the
gateway's level stopped admitting info - so this restores the pre-existing picture rather than
inventing a new one. Anything reading record counts should expect more of them, not different ones:
the templates are the same set.

### D-228 — The embedder's log is held by the runtime, not extended by it

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

semantic-log's LogBase owns the emitter's construction, one logger per component, retention, the
cluster sink and init/stop. blong cannot extend it: load.ts decides a module is a component by
testing 'prototype instanceof Internal', and semantic-log knows nothing of Internal (nor should it).
So SemanticLog still extends Internal and _holds_ a LogBase, and the two hooks it would otherwise
override are LogBaseOptions: 'envelope' (the $meta a call record carries) and 'translate' (reading
$meta out of a call site's arguments). Reconsidering this means changing that detection or marking
the class with system() - not changing the base.

### D-231 — What stayed in blong, and why the boundary is where it is

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

After the move, blong keeps: the $meta envelope (records and call sites), the binds-downwards
logger() contract and ILog's shapes, the call gate (callTrace.ts: config, opt-out patterns, blong
grant), resolveHome/thresholdOf (pino vocabulary). semantic-log owns: LogBase (construction,
per-component loggers, retention store, call-channel plumbing, cluster sink, init/stop), the pino
dialect (logCall.ts), the call channel (capability.ts), the service's start and cluster opener, and
the attachable facade. Two things stayed that a reader may expect to have moved: blong's pino Log
(it writes through pino transports, so the package owns nothing of it) and semanticContext.ts's
identity/leg/participant logic (~250 lines) - that is the framework's dispatch vocabulary, not the
emitter's.

### D-233 — Colour is decided by the intent rather than by the file descriptor

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Playwright starts the backend with stdout piped, so isTTY() is false and the dev block left the
records plain - while the runner relays those same lines into the terminal and colours its own
output beside them. A piped stdout is therefore not evidence that nobody is watching. The playwright
intent now sets log.color true, and a new ci intent (which the same webServer passes last when CI is
set) sets it false again for a run whose output is captured. Verified on the gateway suite: 99 ANSI
escapes in the runners log lines, 0 with the ci intent, and the tap runner passes neither intent so
its plain output is unchanged.

### D-236 — The test-group flow wraps the scenario, not the dispatch

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

A test group answers with its steps and they run afterwards, so the flow had to be minted around the
dispatch and the chain, per group. The alternatives were rejected: one flow for the whole run
interleaves unrelated scenarios into one diagram (the groups run in parallel), and a flow per step
would mint executions no one asked for - a step is not an entry. The groups are therefore run inside
their own flow rather than built first and chained after.

### D-239 — A dispatch hop is declared and recorded by the dispatcher itself

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The hop a dispatch orchestrator forwards is now declared (caller = the namespace it answers for,
i.e. namespaceOf($meta.method), so a shared dispatcher does not credit it to the process) and
recorded through the call channel inside that leg. Recording as well as declaring is the point: the
ledger reads records, and a leg the caller never wrote inside is one it only ever sees as the
callee's receipt. The alternative - emitting a synthetic declaration in the ledger from the leg id -
was rejected: the ledger would be inferring a call nobody made it aware of.

### D-242 — A test group names its flow's phase

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Watch binds the group's display name as the flow's phase around the whole chain (the emitter's step,
exposed through the attachable vocabulary as withStep because blong may not import the emitter
directly). A test group is the entry that owns its flow, and its display name is what a reader sees
in the test list - so the band reads the same as the run does. It is bound around the steps, not
around the dispatch that builds them, because the flow wraps the execution. The vocabulary gained
step for this: the phase mechanism existed, but nothing outside semantic-log could set one.

### D-244 — The public surface declares its calls as `public`, not `gateway`

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The identity the HTTP route declares as the caller of its hop is `public`, not `gateway`. The name
is the logical unit that answered the request - the API surface - and it had to move because
`gateway` is also the namespace the gateway realm answers as: a leg whose caller was `gateway`
calling `gateway.*` drew the surface and that namespace as one participant, and the call as a
self-hop, which is the confusion the name caused in every diagram of that realm. `public` is a unit
of its own: not the process (`blong` - one process hosts a whole suite) and not the namespace being
served. Measured on the gateway realm artifact after the rename: participants `public`, `gateway`
and `db`, with `public->>gateway: public.gateway.bundle.find`, then its answer, then the hop this
realm makes to `db`.

### D-252 — lib.checkpoint is undefined in production, lib.decide never is

> _2026-09-23 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`$meta.checkpoint` is absent in production and `lib.checkpoint` is `undefined` there, while
`$meta.decide` and `lib.decide` are attached in **every** mode. The asymmetry is the point: a
missing point costs a note — and the absent slot is what makes the optional chain free — whereas a
missing branch would skip the work, so `decide` cannot be gated, and a second non-recording variant
would only grow the surface: the recording is a consequence of selecting, not a separate mode. This
is why `createAttachCheckpoint` now always returns an attacher (it used to return `undefined` in
production, so nothing could be attached to a dispatch's `decide`) and why
`Registry._createHandlers` computes `recording` once from `checkpointMode` and uses it for both
`assert` and `checkpoint`.

### D-271 — Allure reporting hangs off the watch config and writes one result per group

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Allure reporting for handler tests is wired in `core/blong-gogo/src/chain.ts`, which is where the
`TestExecutor` for a test group is built, and it is configured under the framework's `watch` key —
the component that runs the groups. CI turns it on and generates the HTML report; a dev run is asked
for it through the same key.

Three decisions are worth keeping.

The test case is the group, not the step. A reader calls the group a scenario ("order checkpoint"),
so one result is written per group when it finishes, with the group's steps nested inside it and the
points and branches those steps announced nested deeper. Writing a result per step as well would
describe the same work twice; `allureResultWrite` still exists for a suite that reports a single
step.

The session is process-scoped and lazy, because `allureSessionStart` clears its results directory: a
per-group session would wipe the groups before it. The first group that runs starts it and the
runner's `endAllureSession` closes it once every group has reported, which is why the ending call
lives in `Watch` (the run owner) rather than in the group runner.

The CLI that generates the report is the one this package depends on, resolved from the package's
own `node_modules` rather than from `PATH`, so results are never rendered by a different Allure than
the one that wrote them.

### D-278 — Every load step is measured and warns past log.slowMs

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Every step of a root load is now measured, and a step that takes longer than `log.slowMs` (default
1000, `SLOW_STEP_MS` in `blong-lib`) is reported at warn level — while it runs, once it crosses the
margin, and again on completion with the elapsed time.

The steps are the suite factory, the config load, layer discovery, every component's import and its
start, and every child realm; import and start are separate labels because an import is the module
graph and a start is the component's own init, and a delayed start that named only `load log` would
not say which to look at. `withProgress` carries the behaviour, so every operation that already
reported progress now also warns when it was slow; its first report lands at the margin rather than
one interval later, which is what makes a slow step visible at one second instead of at five.

The log component is the one step with nothing to log through while it runs — it _is_ the log — so
the loader keeps a bootstrap logger that writes to stderr until it exists. That gap was where the
worst delay hid: nine seconds of nothing, then a burst. The store reports its own slow step through
the logger that is opening it, which is the only channel available at that point and the right one.

`log.slowMs` is the single knob: the loader reads it for its own steps and passes it to the store as
the default for `log.cache.slowMs`. Setting it to 0 turns the warnings off in both.

### D-284 — Allure is guarded on the platform, not on the import failing

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The Allure session is guarded on the platform kind before the lazy import is attempted:
`IChainOptions` gained a `platform` field, `Watch.ts` passes `this.#platform.platform`, and
`canWriteReport()` allows `server` and an absent platform (a direct chain run in Node) while
refusing `browser`. A refusal is reported once per run as a warning that names the platform and says
no report will be produced, and a failed start is dropped rather than left as a rejected session, so
the end of the run has nothing to close and a later group neither awaits a failed promise nor
repeats the message. Rejected alternative: attempt the import and report the failure as a
configuration error, which preserves the accidental case where a browser-flavoured platform loaded
in Node _can_ write the files. It was rejected because the platform is what decides whether the
integration can work at all in a real browser, because the framework's own documentation says a
browser run's results come from the Playwright producer (`allure-results`) rather than this one
(`allure-results-tap`), and because the attempt costs a per-group failure and a dead code path in
the browser bundle for a report that is duplicated in the server load of the same package: the chain
derives `historyId` from the group's full name, so two producers writing the same group read as
retries of one test case rather than as two results.

### D-288 — The EIP chain is reached only through a dynamic import in a browser graph

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Watch.ts now imports the chain for its types and ends the Allure session through a dynamic import,
rather than making @feasibleone/blong-chain's EventEmitter import survive a browser link. Reasoning
the code does not show: the chain is loaded lazily wherever it is used, the group runner imports it
the same way, so nothing gets slower; the browser build already tolerated the edge, so the dev
server's eager link was the only casualty; and a browser-safe base class would have changed emitter
behaviour silently in exchange for keeping a dependency no browser code path needs. The invariant is
guarded by a source scan, src/browserEagerImports.test.ts, because the bundle guard cannot see a
module the loader reaches through a dynamic import — it never enters the built graph.

### D-289 — The captured-run intent is derived from CI, not required from every entry

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The `ci` intent is derived from `isCI()` in `activeConfigs` rather than required from every entry.
Reasoning the code does not show: the intent means the same thing the environment says — nobody
watches this output — and the loader already derives `exit` from `isCI()` in the same assembly, so
an entry that has to remember the intent is a trap for the next package (this one produced no report
for eight packages while the entries that did remember worked). It is appended _after_ the named
intents, which is where a caller that passes it puts it: the Playwright webServer passes `ci` after
`playwright` so the `playwright` block's colours win, and appending it earlier would have flipped
that. The entries that still pass it keep working (the block merges twice identically), and a
package that wants different captured-run settings overrides the block, since the framework's
synthetic blocks merge before the module's own config.

### D-301 — The handler config reads through a versioned live proxy

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The live handler config needed a decision before implementation: what should a live handler config
read through? The handler config is mergeLayerConfig of the module slice (`moduleConfig[name]`) and
the port namespace config (`port.config[namespace]`). Settled and implemented on 2026-09-28. The
decisive fact is that the loader hands the layer the runtime's own config proxy, so the module half
is live by construction and only the copy made it stale: mergeLayerConfig is now wrapped by
ConfigRuntime.liveLayerConfig, which re-merges when ConfigRuntime.version moves and hands the
closure a createConfigProxy instance carrying a before-read hook, so a node destructured at startup
refreshes on its own reads and not only when the root is touched. The port-config re-render half of
the original recommendation was dropped as wrong: re-rendering a port from the values it was started
with is a no-op, and re-rendering it from the runtime slice would discard the context the knex
adapter builds in ready and configChanged. The reload behaviour is asserted through the exported
applyConfigReload in Watch.ts, driven from Watch.test.ts with fake ports.

### D-322 — Every CRUD write case is one transaction, not just the removal

> _2026-09-29 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The removal case was made transactional on its own, and the question that followed — what about add
and edit — was the right one: they had the same shape, several statements on the pool, so a create
could leave a core_resource row with no entity behind it (the ghost resource of T-102, whose name is
then taken for good) and an edit could rename a record and never change the assignments submitted
with it. Both now run in one transaction, and so does merge, which writes the resource rows it looks
up and then the table rows. What made the paths safe in the meantime is worth noting: the edge
writes inside add and edit already went through the transactional syncGraphEdges, so the flattened
paths never disagreed with the graph — the half-applied state was in the record and its details, not
in the authorization view. The remaining gap is realm-side: the access realm's own add and edit
handlers interleave their writes with a call to the db/coreResourceEnsure handler, which uses its
own connection and therefore cannot join a transaction, so making those atomic needs that helper to
become a library function first.

### D-325 — A handler group is reachable from super in its original spelling

> _2026-09-29 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The framework used to store a realm handler group's members on the group's local object under their
normalised names only (methodId lower-cases and strips dots), so the prototype chain a handler
literal inherits from held the lower-cased name and not the camelCase one. `super.<name>` is a
JavaScript property lookup and is case-sensitive, so a camelCase delegation silently resolved to
undefined; only the synthetic procedure handlers were stored under both keys (attachHandlers in
adapter/schema/knex/schemaTable.ts), which is why the docs' super.sqlItemListActive example worked
while super.mathNumberSum did not. layerProxy now stores both spellings for every
handler/model/fixture member, mirroring attachHandlers, and leaves validations on the normalised key
alone because Registry._validations iterates local and a second spelling of each schema would
register a second name for it that methodParts cannot split. Both spellings on one object are
deliberate: findHandler lower-cases what it is given, super does not.

### D-357 — Expected errors now work through the public gateway

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Three changes make a caller's declared failure arrive and be honoured. The RBAC refusal is a typed
error (gateway.notAllowed, gateway.noActions) with the message kept as it was, because matching is
on error.type and a plain Error could never be declared. The JSON-RPC body schema now declares
expect, without which validation stripped the field before the route could read it and the feature
looked unimplemented. And the gateway error handler reads the declaration from the request body,
because a refusal raised in a hook (authentication, RBAC) never reaches the route handler that
resolves expect for the meta. The expectedErrors flag is unchanged and still the security boundary:
the test run enables it through the dev and integration intents.

### D-366 — a namespace Service publishes the RPC port

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · active_

An orchestrator namespace is served by RpcServer on the RPC port, 8091 by default, not on the
gateway port, so the generated per-namespace Service exposes 8091 with targetPort rpc and the
Deployment exposes both rpc (8091) and http (8080) with tcpSocket probes on rpc. GatewayCodec asks
the resolver for `rpc-<namespace>`, so ResolutionK8s strips that prefix and returns
`<namespace>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`. A suite opts in with resolution.impl: kubernetes,
mirroring how the log component picks its implementation.

### D-390 — release replaces prod, and turns the semlog links off

> _2026-10-06 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The new release intent replaces prod rather than sitting beside it: one name for one idea, the
configuration uat, staging and prod share, so what is tested is what ships. It also suppresses the
semlog:// links, which needs a knob of its own because two producers mint them, the semantic refs
and the pino pretty printer, and the semantic package must not be imported at all in that intent. No
alias for prod is kept.

### D-407 — A database with no counters owes no rebuild

> _2026-10-06 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The path refresh drain queries core_counter at startup, and it now answers instead of throwing when
that table is not there: a database with no schema has no counters, so nothing can owe a rebuild,
and a process that was only asked to plan, which is what the k8s intent is, connects to the
deployment database to read its configuration and must not die because the schema has not been
created yet. The match is deliberately narrow, errno 1146 or sqlState 42S02 or ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE,
because a broken connection is a different failure and must still be loud, and both cases are pinned
by a test. The generation run still exits 1 outside a cluster for an unrelated reason: the suites
microservice connection names the host db, which only resolves inside one, so the k8s intent should
eventually not connect at all.

### D-431 — `db` is not an intent; the schema work belongs to `upgrade`

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The framework carried a db intent whose only effect was exit: true, so it named no work at all and a
run that used it connected to the database and did nothing, while the docs described it as database
creation and seeding and the generated migration Job carried it. The user's hint settled it: db was
introduced by accident and caused misalignments, so it is gone from load.ts, from both intent tables
and from the docs, and upgrade is the intent that brings a database up to date. The exit for upgrade
lives in the framework block beside cli and k8s, because when a run is over is the framework's
business, while what the run does is the owning adapter's: schema.sync and schema.seed in the db
adapter of the blong-server realm, the same block being available to any other adapter that declares
it. Alternative considered and rejected: keeping db as a deprecated alias, which leaves two names
for one intent and the ambiguity that produced the misalignment.

### D-432 — Exclusion groups are declared on the entry and refused by the loader

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The framework documented exclusion groups as designed but unimplemented, which left the one
combination worth catching - dev with release - to merge silently, the later block winning wherever
the two overlap. A suite now declares intentsExclusionGroups on its own server() definition, and
loadRealm tests the active intents against every group right after the definition is materialised
and before a single config source merges, so a refused run costs one message that names both
intents. A group allows at most one active member rather than a fixed pair, because the field reads
as pairs either way and a set is what the check needs. Alternatives rejected: warning instead of
refusing, which leaves a process that is neither the one nor the other and merely says so in one
line of startup log; and reading the groups from the merged config, which is only available after
the merge the check exists to prevent. The declaration is a definition field and not a config block
on purpose: no intent should be able to switch off the check that guards it.

### D-442 — The gateway pair is resolved once at load and handed to both readers

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The bridge that defined accessors from gateway.public to remote.client is gone: load.ts resolves the
pair into gateway.sign and gateway.encrypt and copies the same material to remote.client before any
component is constructed, so neither reader has to wait for the other. Load time is what removes the
ordering question the accessors existed for, because the rpc client builds its MLE crypto at
construction and the gateway publishes only when it registers its plugin. A half that nothing
configured is generated here, with the specs and the warning text shared with Gateway.ts, which
keeps the same last resort for a gateway built without the loader. The config is read from
configRuntime.rawSnapshot rather than the proxy, because a read through that proxy returns a path
proxy and resolving one of those writes the path into itself.

### D-443 — The framework prunes the envelope rather than the renderer skipping it

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

semanticRecord.toLogCall lifts mtid and method into the record's own slots and now removes those two
members from fields., dropping the envelope entirely when nothing else is in it. The alternative was
teaching the semantic renderer to skip members the header already shows, which would have left the
duplicate in JSON mode and in the retained store. Members that were not lifted stay, including a
value that is not text, because a method that never reached a slot is nowhere else on the record.

### D-444 — A log line names its caller by message pattern, not for every record

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

log.callSite is a list of regular expression sources matched against a record's message, and a match
adds site, the first frame outside the logging path, to that record. A list rather than a switch
because the interesting line is one particular message and naming the caller of everything buries
it, and nothing is captured for a message that matches none of them. The translation interpolates
pino's printf shape now and always names the caller of a call in it, because no call site in this
repository writes that shape, so one arriving is a dependency's; that is how the fastify bearer-auth
refusal, which logged unauthorized: %s with the reason dropped, was placed. The semantic
implementation matches the formatted message; under pino the match is made where the framework
builds each component logger, because pino has no hook that sees a message.

### D-448 — The mle write-back publishes public halves, not the signing keys

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Asked whether the two lines that write the resolved pair back into `config.sign` and
`config.encrypt` are needed: they are not needed for signing, and the comment that justified them
was wrong. `mle.keys` is the public half of the pair (`core/blong-mle/src/crypto.ts`: `keys` exposes
the PUBLIC JWKs, while `signEncrypt`/`decryptVerify` are bound to the instance's private keys), so
those two lines do not put the process's signing keys on those paths — they put the public halves
there, over the material the loader resolved, which is what the paths hold otherwise. HEAD does not
have them at all: they arrived in an uncommitted session, and `git log -S` finds no commit that
introduced them. Nothing in the framework reads those paths for private material: `Gateway.ts` uses
them for truthiness and hands the same config to the plugin, whose crypto is built before the
write-back runs. The reload question is settled by a test rather than a reading: the gateway
implements no `configChanged`, so the runtime creates the port again (`Watch.ts`), the gateway
merges the incoming config into its own `#config` class field, and the write-back is a property
assignment on that copy — the pair it replaced keeps its private half, so a rebuilt instance
resolves the pair again and can sign. The decision is to keep the lines, with a comment that says
why. One claim had to be corrected rather than kept: this endpoint reading said the lines keep
private material out of "a `/api/sys/config` snapshot", and that endpoint serves
`configRuntime.rawSnapshot` (`SystemDebug.ts`), the merged snapshot itself, where the loader's
material sits with `d`. The fix is at the boundary rather than in the snapshot, because the pair is
legitimately part of the configuration the endpoint exists to show: the route now answers with the
snapshot redacted, and only values that are JWKs lose members (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `k`,
`oth`), so a config property merely named `d` still arrives. The guardrail stands on its own —
`systemDebug` is never enabled in production. Tests hold all of it in `core/blong-gogo/src`:
`mle.test.ts` (the route and the published copy publish no private member, and the write-back
repoints the property while the material it replaced stays intact), `gatewayKeys.test.ts` (a rebuilt
gateway over the same source resolves the pair again and can sign) and `SystemDebug.test.ts` (the
config route serves the pair without its private half and leaves the rest of the configuration
unchanged). F-427 records the misreading that led here.

### D-449 — A separator stays in the wire name and the lump spelling is dropped

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`methodParts` keeps the underscore or hyphen it was given, because the separator is what says which
words form one part and the k8s adapter needs it to rebuild the client spelling. The consequence is
deliberate: a compound kind written as one lump can no longer be split back, so it fails with
`k8s.noMethod` naming the method it built instead of quietly matching nothing, and `METHOD_RESOURCE`
is gone rather than kept as a fallback. Every in-repo wire name, the adapter tables and the realm
`RESOURCE_TYPE_BY_KIND` moved to the separator form in the same change, so nothing in the repository
depends on the old spelling.

### D-497 — A one-off topic read waits for its group assignment

> _2026-10-10 · core/blong-gogo · active_

A one-off `topic.find` now waits for its consumer group's assignment before it reads. The read used
to set a 3s consume timeout and consume immediately from `ready`, but the broker holds a group's
first rebalance for `group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms` (3s by default), so the consume landed before
the assignment and came back empty for a topic that had messages — which is how the commander's
`message` level read empty while `topic.list` listed the topic beside it. `start()` waits for its
own assignment for the same reason, so the read now polls `assignments()` the same way, gets a 5s
consume timeout that covers a fetch, and gives up on a 20s deadline; the promise always settles with
an array, because the caller's contract is "an empty topic, never a malformed RPC response". The
cost is the join itself — roughly 3s per read, since every read uses a fresh group id so that
`auto.offset.reset: earliest` keeps reading from the beginning. The alternative was the seeder's
group-free approach, assigning partitions with explicit offsets, which is faster but needs
per-partition watermarks and reimplements assignment; the group read covers every partition and is
what the rest of the adapter already relies on.

### D-179 — Creator access to a guarded record - decided (b), adapt the specs

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · superseded_

ANSWERED by the user (option b): adapt the specs, keep the enforcement unchanged. Done: the
organization spec now skips create (skipCreate) and edits the seeded organization the signed-in
admin is scoped to; the unit create spec passes unchanged (a unit created without an organization is
unscoped and therefore visible); the portal person-browse spec filters before waiting for the table.
Creator auto-grant (option a) was NOT chosen, so a newly created organization remains invisible to
its creator until a grant names it - the UI New form for party.organization therefore cannot
complete, which is documented in the spec header. Revisit (a) if organization creation must work
through the UI.

### D-240 — A hop's leg id is dotted even when the wire method is slash-routed

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-gogo · superseded_

The dispatch hop declares its leg with legName(forwarded) - the wire method with its separator as a
dot - while the forwarded $meta.method keeps the slash. Slash routing is a transport convention the
receiver strips (methodPath), and the leg grammar flattens a '/' to '-': declaring the slash form
produced gateway.db-gateway.application.register, whose second segment names no participant and
whose target the arrow had to guess at. The dotted id reads as every other leg does,
`<caller>.<target>.<method>`, and the ledger reads the target off it.

Superseded: the hop declares the wire method itself, slash and all (D-249), rather than a dotted
form of it.

Superseded by `D-249`.

The slash is lawful in a leg id now that the id is the method; the caller is no longer part of it,
so there is nothing to flatten away.

### D-276 — Startup silence: visibility change or loader design change

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · superseded_

The startup silence (about 9-10 s before the first log line, and the same load ahead of tap's
output) is pre-existing and has no small fix. Two directions were offered and neither is safe to
take without the user's call:

Making it visible — logging during the component and handler import phase — is a change to the load
pipeline, small but touching the path every start goes through.

Making it faster means loading less eagerly (lazy or parallel handler imports), which is a design
change in the loader with real risk, and the profile says the cost is filesystem latency on a large
number of sequential module operations, so nothing short of that will move it.

The measurements, and the fact that both delays match the stashed baseline, are in the friction
entry about this in the same memory file. Nothing further is being changed until that decision is
made.

The user chose: reclaim automatically and keep the existing directory, a 1s default margin
configurable through the log config, and timing on every operation that reports progress.

### D-440 — linkGatewayKeys is a value bridge between two config paths, not a key source

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · superseded_

The gateway resolves the pair its configuration names and the rpc client reads its own from
remote.client, so nothing connected the two and the client resolved no keys at all in a released
process. The bridge is made of accessors because the gateway resolves at plugin registration and the
client reads lazily on the first call, and a configured pair now wins: the accessor is only defined
where the path is empty, and mle.ts writes the resolved material back to the path it read, so one
reader never holds a recipe while the other holds keys. The channel itself moved with D-441: the
pair travels as an rc document under the pod home rather than as two variables, which is why the
deployment does not have to know any framework variable name.

Superseded by `D-441`.

The channel decision was taken: the pair is an rc document a deployment mounts, so the bridge is
left to the generated-pair case only.
